tei:div.tei:p: The incense was composed of balm, onycha, galbanum, and frankincense, seventy minas’ weight of each; myrrh, cassia, spikenard, and saffron, sixteen minas’ weight of each; twelve minas of costus; three minas of an aromatic bark; nine minas of cinnamon; nine kabs of Karsina lye; three seahs and three kabs of Cyprus wine—if Cyprus wine could not be obtained, strong white wine might be substituted for it—a fourth of a kab of Sodom salt, and a minute quantity of ma‘aleh ashan [a smoke-producing ingredient]. Rabbi Nathan says: A minute quantity of Jordan amber was also required. If one added honey to the mixture, he rendered the incense unfit for sacred use; and if he left out one of its required ingredients, he was subject to the penalty of death.
